title: MaxProof: One Model as Generator, Verifier, Refiner, and Ranker
hook: Treat one model as proof writer, checker, fixer, and judge; search a population of candidate proofs; pick a winner by tournament — enough, the authors report, to clear math-olympiad gold.
key_points: MaxProof trains three skills into one model: proof generation, proof verification, and critique-conditioned proof repair.
Its generative verifier is 'defense-in-depth,' engineered for a low false-positive rate so it doesn't accept wrong proofs.
At test time the same model is generator, verifier, refiner, and ranker — searching a population of candidates and returning one via tournament selection.
This is population-level test-time scaling: spend compute exploring many proofs rather than emitting a single attempt.
Reported to reach 35/42 on IMO 2025 and 36/42 on USAMO 2026, above the human gold-medal threshold on both.
content_html: MaxProof, from the MiniMax-M3 series, tackles competition-level mathematical proof by turning one model into a small proving system. The model is first trained for three capabilities: proof generation, proof verification, and critique-conditioned proof repair, using a "defense-in-depth" generative verifier deliberately tuned for a low false-positive rate — the verifier must not wave through incorrect proofs. These capabilities are then merged into a single released model.
extra_html: At test time, MaxProof is population-level test-time scaling: the model acts as generator, verifier, refiner, and ranker, searches over a population of candidate proofs, and returns one final proof through tournament selection. The authors report that this pushes the M3 model to 35/42 on IMO 2025 and 36/42 on USAMO 2026 — exceeding the human gold-medal threshold on both. The transferable idea isn't the math itself but the recipe: when you have a reliable verifier, you can spend inference compute generating, checking, repairing, and ranking many attempts, rather than betting everything on one. Treat the scores as the authors' reported results.

flashcards.prompt: What four roles does the single MaxProof model play at test time?
flashcards.back_html: Generator, verifier, refiner, and ranker — it produces candidate proofs, checks them, repairs the flawed ones, and ranks them to return a final proof via tournament selection.

flashcards.prompt: Why is MaxProof's generative verifier engineered for a low false-positive rate?

choices.text: So it doesn't accept incorrect proofs as valid
To reduce GPU memory use at inference

flashcards.explanation_html: A verifier that wrongly accepts bad proofs would corrupt the search and tournament selection; a low false-positive rate keeps the selection honest.

flashcards.prompt: What is 'population-level test-time scaling' in MaxProof?
flashcards.back_html: Spending test-time compute to search over a whole population of candidate proofs and select a winner, instead of producing one single attempt.
